A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EHR-ChatQA. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven models on 350 tasks, with repeated trials, interaction statistics, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports evaluations on 366 tasks, revised performance results, and additional empirical analyses of simulator variability and validator reliability.

M1.justification: Tables 5, 7, and 15 refine user termination, validator checks against ground-truth predicates, and requirements for nonempty agent responses. The core agent/tool framework remains. The expanded nested verification-reflection description alone does not establish a new method, since v1 already specifies self-reflection.

E1.justification: Both versions use the MIMIC-IV and eICU demo databases, IncreQA and AdaptQA, and eight corresponding AdaptQA categories. The renamed categories elaborate existing scenarios. Additional AdaptQA instances expand sampling within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same seven models: both Gemini Flash models, o4-mini, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3.3-70B, and Qwen3-32B. GPT-4o-mini was already evaluated in v1 despite its omission from the earlier setup paragraph.

E3.justification: AdaptQA increases from 64 to 80 instances, while IncreQA remains at 286. Table 4 changes both value-search defaults from k=10 to k=100, and simulation-validation prompts are revised. v2 also introduces a randomly sampled 100-trajectory manual audit. The main metrics, temperatures, and action limits remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct validator-reliability audit in Appendix A.4.1, user-turn variability analysis in Figure 4, and three invalidated-trajectory case studies in Appendix D.3. Together these substantially expand scrutiny of the simulation environment beyond the retained agent-failure analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five i.i.d. trials using the same success and consistency metrics. Neither introduces seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new turn-count histogram analyzes simulator behavior rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 extensively revises the central results: o4-mini's IncreQA/AdaptQA SR-5 changes from 81.0/43.8 to 81.3/35.8. Figure 3, interaction costs, and failure percentages also change. New findings include 10% false rejection and 9% false acceptance in the validator audit. Changed settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, binary reward, and performance-metric definitions are retained. Added evaluation examples and explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and central reliability-gap claim remain. The abstract narrows its performance statement to the best-performing agents and revises AdaptQA Pass@5 from 60–80% to 60–70%; numerical gap claims in the introduction and conclusion are also updated.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of validator errors caused by information asymmetry, notes that reflection can introduce different violations, and explicitly limits ground-truth answers to the demo databases. The central interpretations concerning value linking, context management, and inconsistent SQL generation remain.

D1.justification: The appendices substantially expand annotation procedures, value sampling, verification/reflection and rerun feedback, evaluation logic, and beta-tester roles. v2 also corrects eICU schema-mapping documentation and explicitly states that both code and data are public. These additions materially improve implementation transparency without establishing that every newly documented detail changed operationally.

R1.justification: The bibliography, compared prior benchmarks, related-work arguments, and claimed research niche remain unchanged. Reference relocation and formatting do not alter positioning.

P1.justification: Selected passages explaining annotation and interaction flows are rewritten, appendix subsections are reorganized, and category terminology is clarified. Publication headers, an author footnote, and acknowledgments are added. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive diagram refinements, Figure 4 adds two turn-variability histograms, and Figure 3 captions are revised. Tables and figures are relocated or renumbered, while the overall visual design and principal table structures remain.

improvement.justification: The new validator audit and fuller simulation, annotation, and evaluation documentation make the benchmark more transparent and easier to assess. Corrections to schema and results reporting also help. These gains are limited: validator errors remain, and the audit does not establish the claim that false rejection cannot affect performance estimates. Revised scores under changed settings do not themselves demonstrate improvement.
